title: 0514-model-trees-for-identifying-exceptional-players
universal_lens: The logistic-model-tree operator unifies hierarchical clustering and local probabilistic inference. By partitioning the feature space into disjoint manifolds, it applies localized maximum-likelihood estimators to bypass global zero-inflation singularities, yielding a piecewise-differentiable mapping from high-dimensional prospect attributes to bounded success probabilities.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the tree leaves as latent regime clusters within a hierarchical Bayesian framework. Leaf-specific logistic weights act as localized priors for P(plays > 0). Conformal prediction intervals are constructed over these leaf probabilities to quantify epistemic uncertainty in draft value projections.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the model tree dictates state transitions from 'prospect' to 'active roster'. The binary probability threshold governs discrete event triggering. Local regression weights dynamically adjust situational reasoning by quantifying how specific attribute deviations shift an agent's transition likelihood relative to their discovered peer group.

primitives.name: Logistic Model Tree Partition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Logistic regression model tree (LMT): tree partitions feature space on discrete values or learned continuous thresholds; each leaf fits its own logistic regression predicting p_i = P(g_i > 0) (plays at least one NHL game in 7 years).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_i: dimensionless probability of playing at least one game; g_i: integer count of games played (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Feature space can be cleanly partitioned into comparable subgroups; logistic function accurately models the boundary between zero and non-zero outcomes within each leaf.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when subgroup sample sizes drop below the degrees of freedom required for stable maximum-likelihood estimation, leading to overfitting on sparse leaves.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's regime-switching hidden Markov models, where tree paths represent discrete latent states and leaf regressions represent state-emission probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Balanced classification accuracy and Spearman rank correlation against actual games played.

primitives.name: Local Log-Odds Explanation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Explainability: player i's log-odds difference vs group mean = Σ_j w_j (x_ij - x̄_gj); strongest/weakest features = argmax/argmin of w_j(x_ij - x̄_gj) — features that are both predictive (|w_j| large) and unusual for the group.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta \text{logit}_i: dimensionless deviation in log-odds; w_j: dimensionless logistic regression weight; x_{ij}: raw feature value of player i; \bar{x}_{gj}: mean feature value of group g.
primitives.assumptions: Features exhibit approximate linearity in the logit space within the localized leaf; group means provide a valid baseline for comparative evaluation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under severe multicollinearity within a leaf, causing unstable weights w_j and rendering the attribution of feature importance mathematically ambiguous.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical innovation is treating extreme zero-inflation not as a hurdle regression problem, but as a manifold learning task. Global linear models collapse because the gradient signal from the massive cluster of zeros overwhelms the sparse signal from successful players. By employing a CART-like partitioning algorithm, the LMT isolates regions of the feature space where the conditional probability P(g_i > 0 | X) is locally homogeneous. Within each leaf, maximum-likelihood estimation recovers stable logistic weights w_j. This dual approach elegantly decouples the discovery of comparable cohorts from the quantification of individual merit. The explainability operator further projects an individual's feature vector onto the local tangent space defined by the group mean, measuring the Mahalanobis-like distance weighted by the logistic coefficients. This yields a rigorous, non-heuristic justification for why a specific prospect outperforms their peers. However, the method relies heavily on the assumption that historical feature distributions remain stationary. If the underlying talent pool shifts—a regime change—the learned partition boundaries become obsolete, causing sharp drops in predictive accuracy, as observed in the 2008 test split.

The adaptation to logistic regression specifically addresses the zero-inflated count data ubiquitous in sports analytics, echoing earlier hurdle models but retaining superior interpretability through explicit, localized coefficient vectors rather than black-box neural activations. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of a team scout, this model acts as a rational adversary that challenges consensus rankings. It does not merely output a number; it constructs a localized peer group and explicitly enumerates the statistical anomalies that elevate a prospect above that group. It forces the decision actor to confront whether the model's identified 'unusual' features represent genuine untapped potential or mere noise.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto must be applied if the root splits rely exclusively on consensus scouting rankings (e.g., CSS rank), as this introduces circular leakage, essentially teaching the model to mimic human bias rather than discovering independent physical signals. Furthermore, if league-strength confounders (like junior hockey tier) are omitted from the feature set, the resulting leaf groups will be structurally invalid, mixing apples and oranges.
